Confirmed: this is a mise 2026.9.5 bug, not an actual aube provenance downgrade.

With `lockfile_mode = "generate"`, a prior Packslip lock entry containing legacy `provenance = "github-attestations"` is compared against newly generated Packslip metadata, which records the signer but not the generic provenance field. `Some(GithubAttestations) → None` is therefore falsely rejected. I reproduced [Discussion #1528](https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/discussions/1528) exactly.

Both aube 2.2.13 and 2.2.14 Packslips:

- use the same vendor workflow signer;
- are transparency-log recorded;
- report `provenance_linked: true`.

So there is no real trust downgrade.

[PR #13102](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13102) is related because it fixes another failure in the same complete-generation path—unsupported cross-platform Packslip artifacts—but it does not touch the provenance comparison and will not fix #1528.

A safe temporary workaround is:

```sh
MISE_LOCKFILE_MODE=merge mise up aube
```

That uses Packslip’s normal signature/pin verification while replacing the stale generic provenance metadata. The permanent fix belongs in mise, ideally as a focused follow-up to #13102 with this exact regression case. I have not changed code or posted publicly.

I’ll implement this as a focused mise PR from current `main`, with a regression test matching the 2026.9.5 failure. I’ll keep it separate from #13102 unless the code proves the fixes must be stacked, and I’ll leave the existing dirty checkout untouched.
